s: Which one of the following taxes was levied on land and was generally assessed at one-third of the produce, though it could vary from one-tenth to one-half?
x: Kharaj was a land tax, usually assessed at one-third of the produce, with the rate varying according to crop and region from one-tenth to one-half.
tq: Use the nature of the tax to distinguish land revenue from personal and religious taxes.

s:
With reference to taxation during the Sultanate period, consider the following statements:
1. Jizya was imposed on non-Muslims as a poll or protection tax.
2. Zakat was a religious tax payable only by Muslims.
3. Khams represented one-fifth of war booty and treasure-troves due to the state.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. Jizya was a protection tax on non-Muslims, zakat was payable by Muslims, and khams was the state’s one-fifth share of booty and treasure-troves.
tq: Match each tax with both its payer and its nature before selecting the coded combination.
sec: Taxes → nature + payer (kharaj, jizya, zakat, khams, ushr)

s: Ushr was generally associated with which one of the following combinations?
o: Land tax on Muslim-held land and payable by Muslim landholders
Protection tax on non-Muslims and payable by Brahmins only
Religious tax on wealth and payable by non-Muslims
One-fifth share of booty and payable by soldiers
x: Ushr was a land tax imposed at about one-tenth on Muslim-held land and was associated with Muslim landholders. Its rate could be lower on irrigated land.
tq: Discriminate between similar land taxes by identifying the community of the payer.
sec: Taxes → nature + payer (kharaj, jizya, zakat, khams, ushr)

s: Who extended the levy of jizya to Brahmins?

sec: Taxes → nature + payer (kharaj, jizya, zakat, khams, ushr)

s: Under the general sharia arrangement of booty, which of the following was the correct distribution?
o: The state received one-fifth and soldiers received four-fifths.
The state received one-fourth and soldiers received three-fourths.
The state received four-fifths and soldiers received one-fifth.
The state received one-half and soldiers received one-half.
x: Under sharia, khams was the state’s one-fifth share of booty, while the soldiers received the remaining four-fifths.
tq: Separate the standard one-fifth rule from the exceptional policy of particular rulers.
sec: Taxes → nature + payer (kharaj, jizya, zakat, khams, ushr)

s: Which of the following statements regarding booty distribution is correct?
o: All the Sultans uniformly retained one-half of the booty.
Alauddin Khalji and Muhammad bin Tughlaq took four-fifths, while Firoz Tughlaq restored the one-fifth share.
Alauddin Khalji and Firoz Tughlaq took four-fifths, while Muhammad bin Tughlaq restored the one-fifth share.
Firoz Tughlaq took four-fifths, while Alauddin Khalji restored the one-fifth share.
x: Although the sharia rule assigned one-fifth to the state, Alauddin Khalji and Muhammad bin Tughlaq took four-fifths. Firoz Tughlaq restored the one-fifth share.
tq: Track the ruler associated with the deviation and restoration of the standard rate.
